title: Implement rolling SLO suppression to curb alert flapping after capacity regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
A capacity regression on 2026-02-18 triggered a cascade of burn-rate and per-route SLO alerts that created alert flapping and excessive paging for oncall. The postmortem showed three contributing causes: noisy redundant signals (route-level + global burn), overly-sensitive short burn windows that promoted transient spikes to page, and lack of a suppression window after an initial paging event.

Goal:
Design and ship a rolling SLO suppression mechanism and associated signal consolidation rules to reduce pager volume while preserving time-to-detect real degradations. This ticket covers design, feature-flagged rollout, metrics, and runbook updates for oncall responders.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume for SLO-related alerts reduced by >=50% in the first 30 days without increasing time-to-detect P99 latency regressions by >5%
Duplicate alerts (same customer/route fingerprint) must be deduplicated to a single incident in PagerDuty
Feature gated behind 'rolling-suppressions' FF and enabled in staging with synthetic regression tests
implementation_notes: Introduce a per-signal rolling suppression state: when a signal fires a page, suppress subsequent pages for the same fingerprint for a configurable backoff window (default 20m) unless burn-rate exceeds an override threshold
Aggregate related signals into a single incident using a deterministic fingerprint (customer-id + route + signal-type) before creating a page
Add hysteresis to short-burn windows by requiring a sustained burn for 2 consecutive samples (sample interval = 60s) before escalating to page
Expose controls in Console: suppression window, override burn thresholds, deduplication toggle, and per-tenant exemption list
Implement feature-flag and gradual rollout by tenant tier (start with dev/test tenants, then platinum, gold, then all)
testing_plan: Unit tests for suppression state machine and fingerprinting logic
E2E in staging: synthetic capacity regression that previously produced 30 pages -> verify suppression reduces to 1 page and escalation still occurs if burn persists
Chaos test: inject noisy spikes to ensure suppression doesn't mask sustained regressions
Metrics backfill: run offline aggregator over last 90 days to estimate expected reduction and verify thresholds
rollout_plan: Week 1: land server + control-plane changes behind 'rolling-suppressions' FF; no default enabled
Week 2: enable for internal/dev tenants and run synthetic regressions; iterate on thresholds
Week 3: enable for 10% of production tenants (low-impact first); monitor pager volume and false negatives
Week 4: expand to 50% and then 100% with runbook updates and Ops training
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial writeup after postmortem review. Proposed rolling suppression design and initial thresholds based on historical burn distributions.
2026-02-24 - Diego Nguyen: Spike completed for fingerprinting approach. Found edge cases where route parameters varied; normalized fingerprint to include route template instead of full path.
2026-02-27 - Marta Svensson (SRE): Reviewed. Requested conservative default suppression (20m) and an immediate-override when overall cluster capacity drops below 5% remaining.
2026-03-03 - Priya Rao (PM): Approved approach; asked to add Console controls and a clear rollback plan for tenants that observe missed escalations.
2026-03-06 - Diego Nguyen: Server and control-plane changes landed behind FF. Tests added. E2E scheduled in staging for 2026-03-08.
2026-03-09 - SRE/Oncall: Staging synthetic regression validated suppression reduced paging from 14->1 while ensuring a sustained regression still paged within expected SLA.
2026-03-10 - Diego Nguyen: Flag toggles prepared for tiered rollout. Monitoring alerts and dashboards instrumented. Next: 10% production enablement on 2026-03-12.
